verdict.rationale: Bland documents separate development, staging and production environments for every agent. Pathway edits are drafts that do not affect live calls, which keep using the published production version, and versions can be promoted to staging for testing before going live. However, the docs only show that agent configuration is isolated. They do not show that test data such as memory, knowledge, phone numbers or call records is kept apart from production. The testbed re-runs single node interactions, and canary deployments route real production traffic, so neither is a true sandbox. Missing for 10: documented data isolation between staging/dev and production, a test-mode or sandbox API (e.g. test keys or simulated calls with no real telephony), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Every agent has three environments: development, staging and production.
When you edit a pathway, you are working on a draft. Live calls are not affected. They keep using the published production version.
You can also promote a version to staging to test it before it goes live
